literature_proposed.summary: This hole is the Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian theorem, stated exactly in the shape Mathlib's PrimesInAP file once took as a hypothesis (the Prop `WienerIkeharaTheorem`: non-negative f, L-series summable on Re s > 1, L(f, s) − A/(s−1) extending continuously to Re s ≥ 1, hence (Σ_{n<N} f n)/N → A). It is a classical theorem (Wiener 1932, Ikehara 1931) and not in the pinned Mathlib: at the pin the identifier `WienerIkeharaTheorem` does not exist, and Mathlib carries no Tauberian theorem of this strength. A Lean proof exists outside Mathlib, in PrimeNumberTheoremAnd's Wiener.lean (over a newer Mathlib, with the sorries noted on the parent's literature record); the route for this node is a port of that proof as private helpers under the pinned toolchain, which is large. Its sibling hole, the continuation of −ζ'/ζ − 1/(s−1) to Re s ≥ 1, is by contrast a one-line instance of Mathlib's vonMangoldt.LFunctionResidueClassAux at q = 1 (proved, PR #1428).

import Mathlib
open scoped Nat

theorem witness : ∃ (f : ℕ → ℝ) (A : ℝ), (∀ n, 0 ≤ f n) ∧
    (∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re → LSeriesSummable (fun n => (f n : ℂ)) s) ∧
    (∃ G : ℂ → ℂ, ContinuousOn G {s | 1 ≤ s.re} ∧
      ∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re → G s = LSeries (fun n => (f n : ℂ)) s - A / (s - 1)) :=
  ⟨fun _ => 0, 0, fun _ => le_rfl, fun s _ => by simp only [Complex.ofReal_zero]; exact LSeriesSummable_zero,
    ⟨fun _ => 0, continuousOn_const, fun s _ => by simp only [Complex.ofReal_zero, zero_div, sub_zero]; exact (congrFun LSeries_zero s).symm⟩⟩
